name: Phason
desc: A twelvefold dodecagonal quasicrystal of squares and 30/60-degree rhombi built live by the de Bruijn dual, drifting in perpendicular space so that phason flips keep rearranging the tiles beneath a raking light while a narrow annealing front sweeps across the plane.

energy.doc: light contrast + joint weight + front intensity

scale.doc: rhombus edge vs frame (2.2 = a dozen huge tiles, 0.75 = a fine mosaic)

density.doc: engraved hatching richness inside the fat tiles

phason.doc: perpendicular-space drift rate — how often tiles flip in place

front.doc: brightness of the annealing front sweeping the plane

x.doc: tiling centre x as canvas fraction

y.doc: tiling centre y as canvas fraction

style.doc: aesthetic: carved Islamic stucco in raking light / gilt jewel tones on lapis / cold brushed metal plate / luminous additive wireframe on black (non-representational) / flat 3-ink overprint

seed.doc: perpendicular-space phases of the grid families + grain
